text: Flows, actions, and subflows — the three building blocks of every piece of Flow Designer automation you'll ever build. Get fluent with these three, and the rest of this course is just using them with more precision.

Every flow you build is, underneath, a record on the sys_hub_flow table. Structurally it's simple: exactly one trigger that decides when the flow starts, followed by an ordered sequence of actions that run after it. You design it visually, with branches and loops nested in where you need them, but every flow reduces to that same shape — one trigger, then steps.

An action is a single step inside a flow — Create Record, Update Record, Send Notification, Ask For Approval. Each one is defined once as a sys_hub_action_type_definition record, which is what populates the step picker. ServiceNow ships a large library of built-in actions, and when none of them fit, you can build a custom action with its own inputs and outputs — a real scripting skill, covered fully in Chapter 3.

A subflow is still a sys_hub_flow record, the same object as a flow, but it's flagged as a subflow type and isn't meant to be triggered directly. Instead it defines its own inputs and outputs and is built to be called by other flows as a reusable building block — an entire sequence of logic you assemble once and hand to other flows whenever they need it.

Picture it together: a record trigger fires on a new Incident, an action sets a field, a shared subflow handles notification and escalation, and a final action logs the outcome. One trigger, a mix of actions, and a subflow call, all inside one flow record. Next up: the two ways a flow actually starts — record triggers and scheduled triggers.
